judge_assessment.explanation: Both judge observations hold. I recomputed all eight totals from the stems — 3+2=5, 4+3=7, 4+5=9, 6+2=8, 2+6=8, 5+3=8, 3+2+4=9, 4+3+2=9 — and every one matches verify.json and the boxed value in the key. I also checked the two ten-frame drawings against their stems: problem 1's frame is drawn with 3 filled cells and 7 empty, and problem 4's shows a full row of 5 plus 1, which is exactly what the key's 'a full row of 5 and 1 more' says. The 'large work areas, simple language, clear ten-frame models' finding is accurate (3-4 cm per item, 3 pages), and the Quick Answers bank is complete here because every expected value is numeric. The one thing the judge's 32/32 does not account for is a verification gap on problem 6: the sheet prints three fill-in blanks ('___ + ___ = ___') plus the answer line, and verify.json id 6 covers only the total. The item's own skill tag is 'story-to-number-sentence', so the equation the student has to build is the assessed skill, and it is the part that is unchecked.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8's misconception trap is declared and machine-derived, not hand-typed: verify.json id 8 carries traps[{'expr': '4 + 3 + 2 - 1', 'value': 8}], the verifier confirms the wrong method really does yield 8 and that 8 is distinguishable from 9, and the key prints 'If they got 8: counted the starting number as the first count-on'. A grader is told what the error was, not just that there was one.

Problem 5 (2 fish, then 6 more) is written to force commutativity as a strategy — 'Start at the bigger number and count on' — and the key closes the loop by noting that counting on from 2 gives the same answer but takes six counts.

The three study-guide skills map one-to-one onto the worksheet's three skill tags (story-to-number-sentence, count-on-to-add, ten-frame-add) with different numbers in every example and try-it, and the watch-out box names the exact off-by-one that problem 8 traps.

root_causes.description: The verification contract binds one expected value per problem id unless the author volunteers extra entries, so a stem that prints several response slots can ship with only its final value checked. Problem 6 asks the student to build the number sentence and prints three blanks for it, but the JSON records a single solve for the total. Nothing in SKILL.md or in the gate chain compares the count of printed answer slots against the count of verify entries for that id — check_answer_line.py enforces one answer LOCATION per item, not one check per printed blank.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6: 'Write the number sentence for this story, then write the total.' followed by '\makebox[1.4cm]{\hrulefill} $+$ \makebox[1.4cm]{\hrulefill} $=$ \makebox[1.4cm]{\hrulefill}' plus the automatic answer line — four slots.
verify.json id 6: a single {"type": "solve", "expr": "5 + 3 - x", "expected": [8]} — the addend placement is not represented.
The same id is tagged "skill": "story-to-number-sentence", i.e. building the equation is the declared skill of the item.
answer_key.tex problem 6 boxes only \ans{8}; the '5 + 3' half of the finished sentence is prose, so the answer-key binding gate never sees it.

improvements.title: A printed number-sentence slot must carry its own verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Make the rule explicit in SKILL.md's JSON-format section: every blank a student is asked to fill gets a verify entry under that problem's id, using the multi-entry-per-id form that curr-012 already uses (id 8 there carries an eval for the intermediate blank and a compare for the symbol). For this case problem 6 becomes three entries under id 6 — eval 5, eval 3, solve 8 — and the key boxes each with \ans{}. Then add a gate to tests/check_layout.py (which already parses each \problem block) that counts student-fillable slots in the stem — \makebox{\hrulefill}, \underline{\hspace{..}}, \ansblank — and warns at exit 2 when a block's slot count exceeds the number of verify entries for that id.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair for tests/check_layout.py: a worksheet whose problem 6 stem contains three \hrulefill slots plus the automatic answer line, paired with a verify JSON holding one entry for id 6 — the checker must exit 2 and name problem 6 with '4 printed slots, 1 verified'. The same worksheet paired with a JSON holding three entries under id 6 must exit 0. Today the first fixture exits 0, so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic verification gap. The impact on this specific case is modest — problem 6's two addends are transcribed from the stem, so a wrong addend is a copying error rather than a maths error — but the same rule is what catches the substantive instances elsewhere in the shard: curr-034's unverified tens-place digit, curr-051's unverified expanded forms and model values, and curr-062's unverified rounded operands.
improvements.risk: A slot counter is a heuristic over LaTeX and will over-count decorative rules (a \hrulefill used as a signature line, for instance). Ship it at exit 2 (visible warning) rather than exit 1 so a false positive cannot block a correct build, and reuse check_layout.py's existing per-block parser so the two detectors cannot disagree about what a problem block contains.

case_summary: An excellent add-to story set: eight result-unknown stories within 10, all arithmetically correct, with ten-frame drawings that match their stems cell for cell, a machine-derived misconception trap on the closing item, and a study guide whose three sections mirror the three skill tags with fresh numbers. The gap is narrow but real — problem 6 prints a three-blank number sentence and verify.json checks only the total, even though 'story-to-number-sentence' is the item's declared skill. ACCEPT is right; the verification contract should still cover the slot.
